job.style: a clear textbook explanation with one worked example

passage: In geometry, an angle is formed when two rays meet at a common endpoint called the vertex. The size of an angle depends only on the amount of rotation between the two arms, not on the length of the arms themselves. A straight angle measures exactly 180 degrees, forming a straight line, which is indeed a valid angle. When measuring angles, you must always align the protractor’s centre point exactly with the vertex of the angle to get an accurate reading. A reflex angle is specifically defined as an angle greater than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees. For polygons, a triangle is classified as isosceles if it has at least two equal sides, regardless of its orientation or the length of the third side. For example, if a triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm, and 6 cm, it is isosceles because two sides are equal. Furthermore, a square is a special type of rectangle because it possesses all the properties of a rectangle, such as having four right angles and opposite sides that are equal. Understanding these definitions helps us classify shapes and angles correctly without being misled by how they are drawn or positioned on a page.

items.evidence: The size of an angle depends only on the amount of rotation between the two arms, not on the length of the arms themselves.
items.q: Meena makes both arms of a 40-degree angle twice as long. What happens to its size?
items.explain: An angle's size depends only on the turn between its arms, not on how long the arms are.

wrong.why: thinks longer arms make the angle bigger
thinks long arms make the angle look narrower

items.evidence: A straight angle measures exactly 180 degrees, forming a straight line, which is indeed a valid angle.
items.q: Two rays from one vertex point in exactly opposite directions. What do they form?
options: A line that has no angle at all
A reflex angle bigger than 180 degrees
items.explain: Opposite rays make a straight angle of exactly 180 degrees, and it is a valid angle.

wrong.why: thinks a straight line cannot be an angle
thinks any large-looking angle is reflex

items.evidence: When measuring angles, you must always align the protractor’s centre point exactly with the vertex of the angle to get an accurate reading.
items.q: Sita puts the protractor's centre a little along one arm, away from the corner. What happens?
options: Her reading will not be accurate
Her reading will still be correct
Her reading is correct if arms are long
Her reading is correct for small angles
items.explain: The protractor's centre must sit exactly on the vertex; otherwise the reading is wrong.

wrong.why: thinks the centre can go anywhere on an arm
thinks arm length affects the angle
thinks the rule matters only for big angles

items.q: Which of these angles is a reflex angle?
items.explain: A reflex angle is more than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees, so 250 fits.

Equilateral, because all sides look equal
items.explain: Two equal sides make it isosceles, whatever its position or the third side's length.
